# Breadcrumb

> Where this page sits, from the top down. Links to the pages above it, a small chevron between, and this page's name last.

## Install

It lands in `src/rost/breadcrumb/`, with what it needs and its contract. In an app that uses shadcn:

```sh
npx shadcn add https://rost.build/r/breadcrumb.json
```

Then import `src/rost/fonts.css` and `src/rost/tokens.css` once, at the root of the app. More on this in [Install](../INSTALL.md).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | slot |  |  |

## Anatomy

- `root`: A `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` in paragraph type.
- `list`: An `<ol>` in a row that wraps, 4px between its parts.
- `item`: A page above this one: a quiet Link, in the secondary text colour, then a separator.
- `separator`: Rost's chevron-right, 16px, as a mask in the tertiary colour. Hidden from screen readers: the list says the order.
- `current`: This page, in the main text colour. Not a link: `aria-current="page"`.

## When to use

- **Deep pages.** A page three or more levels down, like an invoice inside a client inside a year, so getting back up is one click.

## When not to use

- **The main way around.** Moving between the top sections of an app. That's **Navigation**.
- **Steps.** Steps in a form, one after another. That's a stepper, and Rost doesn't have one yet.

## Behaviour

Every page above this one is a link; this page is last and isn't. On a narrow screen the row wraps. I don't shorten long trails yet: if a trail is longer than four, it probably needs a different structure.

## Accessibility

- **Element**: `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` around an `<ol>`, so it's a landmark and the order is a list.
- **Name**: Breadcrumb.
- **Keyboard**: Tab goes through the links, the way it does through any links.
- **Colour**: The links are 11:1 on the dark page, this page's name 14:1.

## Content

Each page by the name it has on its own page, in sentence case.
